content.text:
I located and analyzed the structure, though with two deviations worth flagging up front.

**The local file wasn't reachable.** `upload_file` failed on `1UBQ.pdb`, `data/1UBQ.pdb`, the absolute working-directory path, and the scratchpad path — I have no filesystem or shell tool to locate it. I substituted the canonical RCSB entry (`https://files.rcsb.org/download/1UBQ.pdb`, 78,570 bytes, SHA-256 `d4a6812d8951cf6594e6a0763f089e35f5a80b62acb3c117b2c5565228a7b161`), uploaded as dataset `f9cad7b01a47213550327a53e373336b` in Galaxy history `bbd44e69cb8906b578bfa3664ec63d7b`. Galaxy's metadata confirms chain A, 602 protein atoms + 58 HET atoms.

**I could not recompute DSSP.** usegalaxy.org has no DSSP/mkdssp tool (`search_tools_by_name` for "dssp" → 0 hits; the only secondary-structure tool is EMBOSS `garnier`, a sequence-based GOR prediction, which says nothing about *this* set of coordinates). I wrote a Kabsch–Sander implementation as a containerized user tool, but Galaxy rejected it: `403 "User is not allowed to run unprivileged tools"`. So the numbers below come from the **depositor's own HELIX/SHEET annotation in the PDB file**, not from a re-derivation off the coordinates.

Those records were extracted with Galaxy tool `Grep1` (Select, v1.0.4), job `bbd44e69cb8906b50f90f21dfcffecda`, output dataset `f9cad7b01a4721358c20e40232c05a07`:

```
HELIX    1  H1 ILE A   23  GLU A   34  1        12
HELIX    2  H2 LEU A   56  TYR A   59  5         4
SHEET    1 BET 5 GLY A  10  VAL A  17  0
SHEET    2 BET 5 MET A   1  THR A   7 -1
SHEET    3 BET 5 GLU A  64  ARG A  72  1
SHEET    4 BET 5 GLN A  40  PHE A  45 -1
SHEET    5 BET 5 LYS A  48  LEU A  50 -1
```

Helix class `1` = right-handed α; class `5` = right-handed 3₁₀. Sheet sense `-1` = antiparallel, `1` = parallel, so BET is a **mixed** five-stranded sheet. Chain length is 76 residues (`DBREF 1UBQ A 1 76`, UniProt P62988 UBIQ_HUMAN; SEQRES = 76).

Percentages below are my arithmetic over those ranges and the 76-residue chain:

| Element | Residues | Count | % of 76 |
|---|---|---|---|
| α-helix | 23–34 | 12 | 15.8% |
| 3₁₀-helix | 56–59 | 4 | 5.3% |
| **all helix** | | **16** | **21.1%** |
| β-strand β1 | 1–7 | 7 | |
| β-strand β2 | 10–17 | 8 | |
| β-strand β3 | 40–45 | 6 | |
| β-strand β4 | 48–50 | 3 | |
| β-strand β5 | 64–72 | 9 | |
| **all β-sheet** | | **33** | **43.4%** |
| unassigned (loop/turn/coil) | | 27 | 35.5% |

Caveat on interpretation: depositor HELIX/SHEET ranges for 1UBQ are somewhat more generous at strand termini than DSSP would be, so a true DSSP run would likely shift a few residues from E into T/S/coil. Treat 43.4% β as an upper bound. I did not compute that difference and will not guess at it.

## ANSWER

PDB 1UBQ (ubiquitin, chain A, 76 residues) — from the deposited HELIX/SHEET records:

- **Helix: 16 residues, 21.1%** — one α-helix (23–34, 12 res) + one 3₁₀-helix (56–59, 4 res)
- **β-sheet: 33 residues, 43.4%** — five strands (1–7, 10–17, 40–45, 48–50, 64–72) in one mixed sheet
- **Loop/turn/coil: 27 residues, 35.5%**

Source: depositor annotation in `1UBQ.pdb` (RCSB), extracted via Galaxy `Grep1` job `bbd44e69cb8906b50f90f21dfcffecda`. This is a lookup, not a DSSP recomputation — no DSSP tool exists on usegalaxy.org and custom tool creation was denied (403).
